# Linux Developer Cheatsheet (RAG seed document)

## Process and resource inspection
- List processes by CPU: `ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head`
- Kill a process: `kill -9 <PID>` (irreversible tier — confirm first)
- Live system monitor: `htop` or read `/proc/meminfo` and `/proc/cpuinfo`
- Disk usage by directory: `du -sh *` or `ncdu`
- Battery percentage: read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`

## systemd services
- Status: `systemctl status <unit>`
- Restart: `systemctl restart <unit>`
- User services live in `~/.config/systemd/user/` and start with
  `systemctl --user enable --now <unit>`

## Git workflow
- Stage and commit: `git add -A && git commit -m "message"`
- New branch: `git switch -c feature/name`
- Push: `git push -u origin HEAD` (irreversible tier if force-pushing)
- Undo last commit but keep changes: `git reset --soft HEAD~1`

## Python environments
- Create a venv: `python -m venv .venv`
- Activate: `source .venv/bin/activate`
- Install from lockfile: `pip install -r requirements.txt`

## Search and files
- Fast content search: `rg "TODO"` (ripgrep)
- Find files modified today: `find . -mtime -1 -name "*.py"`
- Locate by name: `locate <name>` (uses the mlocate database)

# OSAIMA — Frequently Asked Questions (RAG seed document)

## What is OSAIMA?
OSAIMA (OS AI Management & Automation) is a voice-first, on-device AI operating
system interface for Linux. An on-device LLM agent listens, reasons, and acts as
the primary shell, replacing the traditional GUI-and-CLI paradigm. All audio and
context data stay on the device — there is no cloud dependency.

## How do I run the tests for an OSAIMA subsystem?
Each subsystem ships a pytest suite. From the subsystem directory:
```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pytest -q --cov
```

The intent router target is greater than 92% classification accuracy on the
held-out 1000-utterance test set.

## Which local LLM should I use?

least 6 GB of free RAM. On low-resource devices with 4 GB RAM, fall back to
Phi-3-mini-4k-Instruct. Pull a model with:

## How does the intent router decide fast path versus slow path?
A keyword trie matches roughly 200 common commands in under 50 milliseconds; a
hit dispatches directly over D-Bus. A miss goes to a fine-tuned BERT-tiny model
that classifies the utterance into one of three tracks — system command,
workflow generation, or content generation — plus 40 system intents.

## What stops a dangerous command from running?
Every LLM-generated command is classified into a risk tier: read-only commands
auto-execute, reversible commands need a single-click confirmation, and
irreversible commands (rm -rf, format disk, git push) require type-to-confirm
with a preview. Generated scripts run inside a systemd transient scope with all
capabilities dropped, private tmp, and no new privileges.
